events.type: background: China export controls on indium phosphide
events.summary: AXT makes most of its wafers in China through its subsidiary Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology. On 2025-02-04 China added indium phosphide (InP) substrates to its export-control list, so every shipment abroad needs a permit from China's Ministry of Commerce. Q2 2025 revenue fell to $18.0 million (down 35.6% year on year). Tongmei began receiving permits for some customers in Europe and Japan (8-K, 2025-06-11), and Q3 2025 revenue recovered to $28.0 million, well above guidance, after permits were granted. Permits for US customers are still not issued: the April 2026 prospectus said they were 'in the final stages of review but has not yet been issued', and the Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-13) says 'InP export permits represent the most significant challenge we currently face' and 'we still cannot predict when a permit application will be reviewed and approved'.
events.why_it_matters: This is the single biggest risk and the single biggest possible upside: AXT can only sell abroad what Beijing allows it to ship. Any US permit would unlock backlogged orders; any tightening would cut sales.

events.summary: AXT filed an automatic shelf registration (S-3ASR) and sold 8,560,311 new shares at $64.25 in an underwritten offering led by Northland, raising $549,999,981.75 gross ($522.5 million before expenses). Shares outstanding rose from 55,578,827 to 64,139,138 (about +15.4%). Stated use: fund Tongmei's InP capacity expansion, R&D, working capital. Same day AXT pre-announced Q1 2026 revenue of $26-28 million.
events.why_it_matters: Each existing share now owns a smaller slice of the company, but AXT now has the cash to triple InP capacity. The automatic shelf means AXT can sell more shares quickly in future.

Events during the fall: (a) insiders sold heavily in early-to-mid June at $88-$115, none flagged as pre-planned 10b5-1 trades: CEO Morris Young sold 197,498 shares on 2026-06-01/02 (about $22.3 million, partly from exercising 2016 options; he still held 2,149,533 shares), director Jesse Chen about $4.4 million across June, director David Chang about $0.9 million, director Leonard LeBlanc about $0.6 million (June-August); (b) on 2026-06-26 Tongmei withdrew its long-pending Shanghai STAR Market IPO to refocus on Hong Kong, which gives 11 Chinese private-equity funds the right to ask for their RMB 324,404,508 (about $49 million) back; AXT says it has the cash to repay in full; (c) on 2026-07-02 the stock fell 15.8% in a broad chip sell-off. No single published cause for the whole decline was found.
events.why_it_matters: Shows how violent this stock is: it lost three-quarters of its value in two months without the business deteriorating. A beginner should expect swings like this again.

events.type: background: Lumentum contract, record Q2, big guidance, index inclusion
events.summary: After the close on 2026-07-29 AXT disclosed a six-year capacity reservation agreement (signed 2026-07-26) with Lumentum: an initial $43.5 million deposit within 30 business days and a second $43.5 million deposit to be set during 2028, applied as credits against future wafer purchases, with Lumentum paying for any shortfall below its annual commitment. On 2026-07-30 AXT reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $47.6 million (up 164% year on year), InP revenue of $30.7 million, GAAP gross margin 44.9%, GAAP net income $11.1 million ($0.17 per diluted share), and guided Q3 to $66 million revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $0.30-$0.32, versus analyst consensus of about $38.7 million and $0.10. The stock rose 27.0% on 2026-07-30 and 28.7% on 2026-07-31. On 2026-09-16 S&P Dow Jones Indices said AXT would join the S&P SmallCap 600 (effective before the open 2026-09-21); the stock rose 11.4% that day.
events.why_it_matters: This is the core of the bull case: big optical-component makers are paying in advance to lock up AXT's InP supply, and revenue is stepping up fast. Index inclusion forces index funds to buy the shares.

why_chain.text: Why is the stock up about 1,700% in a year? Because revenue went from $18.0 million (Q2 2025) to $47.6 million (Q2 2026) with $66 million guided for Q3, as AI data centers buy more optical lasers made on InP wafers.

Why do AI data centers need InP? The lasers and light detectors inside high-speed optical transceivers (the plug-in modules that turn electrical signals into light between servers) are built on indium phosphide wafers; AXT's CEO attributes the 'step-function increase in our revenue' to 'strong customer demand for data center optical connectivity'.

Why is supply tight? Few companies make InP substrates, AXT's capacity was about $20 million a quarter at the start of 2026, and customers (Lumentum, Coherent) are paying deposits to reserve capacity; China's export permits further limit how much can leave China.

Why is it 40% below its high? It overshot to $140.83 in May, then fell 74% amid heavy insider selling, the Tongmei IPO withdrawal and chip sell-offs, before recovering on the Lumentum deal and Q3 guidance. No source gives one cause for the May-July drop; momentum trading and valuation are the likeliest explanation.

products.name: Indium phosphide (InP) substrates
products.what_it_is: Thin, polished discs (wafers) of indium phosphide crystal on which other companies build lasers and light detectors.
products.analogy: AXT sells the blank canvas; companies like Lumentum and Coherent paint the laser onto it.
products.buyers: Makers of optical components and transceivers for AI and cloud data centers (named customers with supply deals: Lumentum and Coherent in the US, Casella in China), plus telecom and sensing.
products.how_it_works: AXT grows a single crystal of InP in a furnace, slices it into wafers, and polishes them. Customers grow thin layers on top to make lasers that send data as light at very high speeds; InP emits light at the wavelengths used in fiber, which silicon cannot do well.
products.sales: Q2 2026 InP revenue $30.7 million (company record), about 64.5% of total revenue of $47.6 million; order backlog 'exceeding $100 million'. Unit volumes not disclosed.
products.sales_source: AXT Q2 2026 earnings call, 2026-07-30 (Motley Fool transcript https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/03/axt-axti-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ ; Semiconductor Today 2026-08-04 https://www.semiconductor-today.com/news_items/2026/aug/axt-040826.shtml). InP revenue is not broken out in the press release itself.
products.stage: shipping and ramping; capacity about $35-40 million per quarter targeted for Q3 2026, about $60 million by end-2026, about $130 million by end-2027 (management targets)
products.size_for_company: Majority of revenue (about 64.5% in Q2 2026). The $130 million per quarter capacity target would be about 2.7x total Q2 2026 company revenue.
products.competition: Other InP substrate makers outside China (in Japan and Germany, per NTD 2026-09-08 report, e.g. Sumitomo Electric; JX Advanced Metals) who do not need Chinese export permits; IQE's CEO called InP substrate access 'an emerging industry supply risk'.
products.why_investors_care: It is the bottleneck material for AI optical links; AXT is one of few large suppliers and customers are prepaying for capacity.
products.watch_next: Q3 InP revenue on 2026-10-29; whether US export permits are granted; whether capacity hits the $60 million per quarter end-2026 target.

products.name: Lumentum capacity reservation agreement (contract)
products.what_it_is: A six-year contract in which Lumentum reserves a minimum yearly amount of AXT's InP wafer output.
products.analogy: Like paying a large deposit to a builder to hold your spot in a long waiting list; the deposit is later spent on the actual goods.
products.buyers: Lumentum Operations LLC (a US maker of lasers and optical transceivers).
products.how_it_works: Lumentum pays $43.5 million within 30 business days and a second $43.5 million to be set during 2028; deposits are used as credits against future purchases; if Lumentum buys less than its annual commitment it pays the shortfall (exceptions: force majeure, quality).
products.price: not disclosed (per-wafer price and annual committed volume not disclosed)
products.sales: Total contract value not disclosed; deposits total $87.0 million (2 x $43.5 million).
products.stage: signed 2026-07-26; first deposit due within 30 business days
products.size_for_company: The $43.5 million first deposit is about 91% of AXT's Q2 2026 quarterly revenue ($47.6 million).
products.competition: Coherent signed a similar deal (about $25.4 million prepayment/commitment, per Semiconductor Today 2026-08-04); exact terms differ.
products.why_investors_care: A customer committing cash for six years is strong evidence the demand is real, not hype. Note: the agreements list Chinese export permits among risks the parties will review (NTD, 2026-09-08).
products.watch_next: Whether the first deposit was received (Q3 10-Q, due about mid-November 2026) and whether US export permits allow shipments to Lumentum's US sites.
